\\]\\s*\\[(?<index>\\d+)\\]\\s+(?<name>.+)$
Explanation:
○ Match ']'.

○ Match '['.
○ "index" capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match ']'.
○ Match a whitespace character greedily at least once.
○ "name" capture group.
○ Match a character other than '\n' greedily at least once.

○ Match ']'.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically at least once.
○ Match '"'.
○ "name" capture group.
○ Match a character other than '"' atomically at least once.
○ Match '"'.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match a whitespace character atomically at least once.
○ Match '('.
○ "kind" capture group.
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "video".
○ Match the string "audio".
○ Match the string "none".
○ Match ')'.
○ Match a whitespace character greedily any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:SixBench.Services.Streaming.AnnexBParser
member.summary: Incrementally splits an H.264 Annex-B byte stream into access units.
member.remarks: A new access unit begins at an AUD, SPS, PPS or SEI NAL, or at a slice whose first_mb_in_slice is 0, once the current unit already contains a picture slice. Because a unit is only known to be complete when the next one starts, output lags input by one frame. The latest SPS/PPS are cached and inserted ahead of any IDR that lacks them, so every keyframe unit can start a fresh decoder.
